overview: The week of August 3–10 was among the most active in recent bpf-next history, with approximately 100 patches across 20 patch series touching nearly every layer of the BPF stack. Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi's 14-patch series (v5) adds __arena and __arena__nullable argument support to kfuncs and struct_ops, enabling BPF programs running on arena memory to hand arena pointers directly to kernel functions while the JIT handles the necessary address rebasing. Yonghong Song's 13-patch series extends the verifier, JIT, and precision-backtracking machinery to support aggregate return values up to 16 bytes via the R0:R2 register pair, a prerequisite for kfuncs that return struct-by-value. Leon Hwang introduced the tracing_multi link type for attaching a single tracing program to multiple kernel functions at once, and Mahe Tardy's bpf_ksock series adds a kernel socket management API so BPF programs can initiate outbound connections from within the kernel.

patches.title: bpf: Support __arena and __arena__nullable kfunc argument suffixes
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: Adds verifier and JIT support for the __arena and __arena__nullable parameter suffixes on kfunc declarations, allowing arena-backed pointers to be passed from BPF programs to kernel functions. The verifier checks that the pointer originates from an arena map and the x86 JIT emits the required address-rebasing sequence before the call. The companion patch extends the trampoline for struct_ops to perform the same rebase for methods that accept arena arguments. The 14-patch series (v5) also fixes a latent bug in stack-passed arguments for indirect trampolines and adds comprehensive selftests covering JIT-sequence correctness, nullable pointers, and attach-rejection for tracing/freplace programs targeting arena struct_ops.

patches.title: bpf: Add verifier support for 16-byte returns in R0:R2
patches.author: Yonghong Song
patches.summary: Extends the BPF verifier to understand register-pair returns (R0:R2), allowing kfuncs whose C return type is a struct of up to 16 bytes to be correctly modelled during verification. The series wires up JIT support on x86 and arm64, adjusts precision backtracking and live-register analysis to account for R2 as a second return register, and adds a guard that rejects register-pair returns when the subprog's BTF information is unavailable. Earlier patches factor out helper utilities and explicitly reject callbacks that attempt to return more than 8 bytes. The 13-patch series (v3) includes a comprehensive selftest suite covering C structs, inline assembly, subprog calls, and callback edge cases.

patches.title: bpf: Add tracing_multi link support for bpf progs
patches.author: Leon Hwang
patches.summary: Introduces BPF_LINK_TYPE_TRACING_MULTI, a new link type that allows a single BPF tracing program to be attached to multiple kernel functions in one operation. The implementation extends the trampoline infrastructure with a multi-target attach path, adds fdinfo and bpf_link_info reporting for the new type, and teaches libbpf how to create and manage tracing_multi links. The 13-patch series includes selftests for attach, rollback, cookie retrieval, and tailcall interaction with fentry.multi, covering the full lifecycle of the new link type.

patches.title: bpf: Add ksock kfuncs
patches.author: Mahe Tardy
patches.summary: Introduces a bpf_ksock kernel object and accompanying kfuncs that allow BPF programs to create, connect, send data on, and close TCP/UDP sockets from within the kernel, without going through the full socket syscall path. A prerequisite net patch adds a connect_socket() helper that the kfuncs build on. The series (v5) restricts attachment to non-LSM hook points to prevent privilege escalation, and includes tests for the kfunc operations, a forbidden LSM attach test, and an async callback guard test using the ksock API.

patches.title: bpf: infer zext_dst based on static register liveness analysis
patches.author: Eduard Zingerman
patches.summary: Replaces the BPF verifier's heuristic zext_dst (zero-extension destination) annotation with one derived from a static liveness analysis over register upper halves. The current approach conservatively inserts zero-extension fixup instructions whenever the destination register might be read as 64-bit, but the static analysis can prove many of these unnecessary, reducing the number of injected instructions in the fixup pass. Supporting patches extract helper utilities, move bpf_is_reg64() to fixups.c, track upper 32-bit register-half liveness in compute_live_registers(), and simplify the resulting bpf_is_reg64() logic. The 7-patch series (v4) includes selftests that verify the new annotations against a range of instruction types.

patches.title: bpf: Show more useful info in stack depth stats
patches.author: Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi
patches.summary: Improves the verifier's per-subprogram instruction statistics output, making it easier to understand which subprograms dominate verification cost. The series (v7) tracks instruction counts separately for each subprogram rather than aggregating into a single total, attributes async callback instructions to their verification roots rather than the main program, and updates veristat's stack-depth parsing to handle the richer output format. Together these changes make veristat substantially more useful for diagnosing programs with long verification times caused by a single hot subprogram.

patches.title: bpf: Add a sleepable page allocator for map memory
patches.author: Jiayuan Chen
patches.summary: Introduces a sleepable page allocator for BPF map memory as a prerequisite for handling arena fault-in correctly when the cgroup memory limit (memory.max) is in effect. When the arena's fault handler runs inside a memory-constrained cgroup, the previous non-sleepable allocator could not perform reclaim or invoke the OOM killer. The series (v3) moves fault-in page allocation outside the arena lock to allow sleeping, adds a read_cgroup_file() utility to cgroup_helpers, and includes a selftest that triggers arena faults under a tight memory.max constraint to verify correct reclaim behaviour.

patches.title: mm/bpf: Add bpf_try_to_free_mem_cgroup_pages kfunc
patches.author: Hui Zhu
patches.summary: Adds a new kfunc bpf_try_to_free_mem_cgroup_pages() that allows a BPF program to proactively trigger page reclaim for a specific cgroup, enabling BPF-driven memory management policies. The series also introduces bpf_thread_wq, a kthread-backed workqueue variant that executes BPF work items within a chosen cgroup's context, making it possible to schedule cgroup-aware reclaim work from BPF. Selftests cover async reclaim via bpf_wq and bpf_thread_wq as well as thread_wq cgroup placement semantics.

patches.title: resolve_btfids: Deduplicate BTF after btf2btf transformations
patches.author: Ihor Solodrai
patches.summary: Extends resolve_btfids with BTF deduplication after its btf2btf transformation pass, preventing duplicate type entries that could cause mismatches when the kernel loads the resulting BTF. Subsequent patches in the series (v3) teach resolve_btfids to process KF_ARENA_* flags and emit the corresponding arena type tags, and to emit bpf_kfunc and bpf_fastcall decl tags automatically based on the source annotations. Documentation and selftests verify the emitted tags round-trip through BTF correctly. This work is closely related to Kumar Kartikeya Dwivedi's arena-argument kfunc series.

patches.title: bpf: Compare iterator types during state pruning
patches.author: Ning Ding
patches.summary: Fixes a verifier state-pruning bug where two states with different BPF iterator types but otherwise identical register values could be incorrectly considered equivalent, potentially allowing an unsafe program to pass verification. The fix adds iterator-type comparison to the state equivalence check used during pruning so that states carrying different iterator kinds are not merged. A companion selftest exercises RCU iterator state pruning to confirm the fix prevents incorrect pruning in practice.

patches.title: bpf, tcx, netkit: reject offloaded programs
patches.author: Jiayuan Chen
patches.summary: Closes a safety gap where BPF programs compiled for hardware offload could be attached on the host via tcx or netkit and run without the expected hardware context. The fix centralises the offload check in dev_xdp_install() and propagates rejection through the tcx and netkit attach code paths, preventing hardware-only programs from silently running in the kernel. A selftest verifies that dev_xdp_install() now correctly rejects device-bound programs when no offload device is present.

patches.title: bpf, x86: Fix exception table metadata for arena load-acquire
patches.author: Daniel Borkmann
patches.summary: Corrects the x86 JIT's exception table metadata generation for arena load-acquire instructions, ensuring that the extable entries point to the correct fixup handlers when an arena access faults. A companion patch makes the same fix for arm64. The series (v2) also adds a verifier-side rejection of load-acquire from pointer types that require fault protection but cannot tolerate the exception-table based fault recovery, and includes selftests for both the arena fault path and the probe-memory pointer type rejection.
